places.name: Nørre Lyndelse, Funen
places.what: Born in a cottage at Sortelung, in the parish of Nørre Lyndelse, the seventh of twelve children. The cottage no longer stands; a memorial stone marks the site. Coordinates mark the village.

places.name: Nørre Lyndelse, Funen
places.what: Grew up in the parish. He played the violin from the age of six, herded geese at Bramstrup from eight or nine, and had lessons from the assistant teacher Emil Petersen. By 1879 the family had moved to a house called Petersborg, which is now a museum.

places.name: Odense
places.what: Military musician with the Sixteenth Battalion, from 1 November 1879, with violin lessons in the town. He left at the turn of 1883–84 for the Copenhagen Conservatory.

places.name: Dresden
places.what: Heard Wagner’s Ring on his first stay in Germany, on an Ancker grant; his diary of 10 September records Das Rheingold. He left for Berlin on 18 October.

places.name: Berlin
places.what: Met Sibelius, Christian Sinding and the violinist Joseph Joachim. Through the winter he divided his time between Berlin, Leipzig and Dresden, and left for Paris at the end of January 1891.

places.what: Arrived on 26 February. At a party at the Bendix home on 1 March he met the sculptor Anne Marie Brodersen, and by 16 March they had decided to marry.

places.name: Gothenburg
places.what: Guest conductor with the Gothenburg orchestra in the 1921–22 season, after an engagement in autumn 1918. He had begun the Wind Quintet before leaving Copenhagen for Gothenburg on 1 February 1922 and finished it here in April. He conducted the Fifth Symphony on 8 March 1922, and the quintet was first played in private on 30 April.
